$comment: Cases for logic that exists in both TypeScript and Python, because the Python adapter cannot import core. packages/selenium-devtools/tests/mirror-vectors.test.ts runs every section against the TypeScript implementation and packages/selenium-devtools-py/tests/test_mirror_vectors.py against the Python one, so a case added here checks both and a one-sided change fails the other language's run. Both runners refuse a section they do not know. Test data only: nothing under src imports it, and the package is private.

notCovered.screencastBufferThinning: Deliberately different algorithms. core's ScreencastRecorderBase halves its buffer keeping first and last; the Python push recorder (screencast.py) also thins incoming frames by its decimation stride and holds the newest skipped frame for the tail, because halving alone drifts toward the end of a pushed stream (CLAUDE.md, the pushed-screencast entry). There is no shared output to state.

waitPollKeys.notes: polls are the evaluations of one wait's condition; each issues its calls in order. expect gives each call a group name: two calls share a poll key exactly when they share a name. outsideWait calls are issued with no wait running and have no key. Object arguments are not covered: Python sorts their keys and TypeScript keeps insertion order, which only differs when one call site builds the same object in two orders.

secretRedaction.notes: Every string in a JSON-shaped value has each secret (listed or typed) replaced by the fixed placeholder, in five forms: as typed, JSON-escaped, encodeURIComponent, form-encoded (space as +, only alphanumerics and *-._ kept) and XML-escaped (& < > " as & < > ", ' left as it is, the way a native page source carries an attribute). Typed passwords are redacted exactly like listed secrets; a keystroke prefix of either is never replaced, since the page collector already masks a password field's own value keystroke by keystroke. An array of 4 or more one-character strings (a W3C Send Keys value) is redacted as the text it spells and split back into characters, so it takes the placeholder's length. A data: URI or a base64 run of 256+ characters is left alone unless it equals a form of a secret, and so is any string under `screenshot`, or under `data` beside a `mimeType`. With `authHeaders` (on whenever input masking is), the values of Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie in any object under `headers`, `requestHeaders` or `responseHeaders` are replaced, a string under `cookies` has each cookie's value replaced, and a cookie object (string name and value plus a W3C cookie field) has its value replaced. Keys are kept. A value that changes nothing is returned as it is.

typedSecret.notes: What input masking adds to the run's secrets when a key-sending command types into a field: the typed text (string and number parts joined, WebDriver's special keys U+E000..U+F8FF removed) when it is at least 4 characters after trimming and the field's type reads `password` (trimmed, any case) or the read did not answer (`answered: false`: it failed, hung past its ceiling, or the field could not be located), since redacting a non-password is the safer error. A read that answered with no type (`fieldType: null`) is not a password. `redacts` is that decision; each adapter only supplies the field-type read.
